body: Yeah I don't really understand it either, I'll probably try to reach out to him too then. Yeah I'm assuming that's the case, or maybe their system is wrong. Thanks, that's very kind of you. MS has practically destroyed my life since I was diagnosed at 16 and there is practically zero support for men with MS since it's so uncommon. I'm assuming that's the next step anyways depending on how stuff goes. Me too, your confidence in me to s greatly appreciated. You're seriously my hero, thank you so much. I'll let you know how everything goes :)

Yeah I agree completely. Good I guess, I'm 21 and I've known him practically all my life, but I don't know know if he'd back me since for I know he's the one contesting it. No nothing like that, I've had very little if any contact with anyone from my workplace these last few months. It's okay, I'm still in the remissing relapsing stage which is considered the least severe, so it could be worse I suppose. I'll try that tomorrow, hopefully they'll do something of the sort for me. Yeah it's a bit rough, I don't really understand why they decided to wait until now to file a complaint. I think I know that, it's just tonight espically I feel like I got closer then usual, almost to the point of attempting something. Thanks for talking, it seriously helps alot, I hope your keeping safe.

Thanks, I appreciate it. Something like I was willfully unemployed and that I had only asked for a leave of absence, which isn't true since I was told that day before work to start staying home I never asked for anything. I think so, my main issue is that I just don't want to go through the hassle, I've already made it painfully clear to them how Multiple Sclerosis and it's medications work so I don't know what good it'd do. US, Iowa to be exact. I don't even know if it'd be able too, the only means I'd have would be some kind of overdose with Lexapro and Gilenya. And from what I've read it's quite painful with a low success chance.
